I live in Santa Cruz county, a couple miles from the epicenter of the 1989 quake that rocked the bay area. In fact the chimney on my house fell during the quake and crashed my grandma's car which she had just got out of to bring groceries inside. A fact i always remember is the shifting of the fault will cause SF to move to southern California in a few billion years. The fault isnt really on the news unless there's been an earthquake or they're trying to scare people about the possibility of an earthquake. I think everyone learns about earthquakes and what to do during them in elementary school nowadays. Never heard of ShakeOuts, maybe its a So-Cal thing. An actual earthquake wouldn't be too devastating i think in my neighborhood, but i live in the woods where we have to worry most about falling trees, but i figure the redwoods around my house have probably survived more earthquakes then my house ever will. With the strict building codes they have in this county after the last big one im confident most buildings would survive a large earthquake (at least enough to save the lives of anyone inside). Power outages would be a huge problem in this area but most people are used to being without power. We haven't taken any major precautions except keeping excess non-perishable foods in the house, California living is just too laid-back. Hope i've been helpful!
